title: Maximum capacity: two-pointer greedy search
summary: Start with a pointer at each end. For each pair of walls, compute the capacity, keep the largest seen, and move the pointer at the shorter wall inward. The maximum is 28.
context: Given wall heights ht = [3, 8, 5, 2, 7, 7, 3, 4] (indices 0 to 7), container capacity is cap[i, j] = min(ht[i], ht[j]) × (j - i).

Initialize left pointer i = 0, right pointer j = 7, and maximum capacity res = 0. While i < j, compute current capacity cap, update res = max(res, cap), compare the two wall heights, and move the pointer on the shorter wall one step inward until i and j meet.
description: Across 9 steps, teal label i and blue label j sit above the selected left and right walls highlighted in matching colors; in Steps 2 through 8, the current container between them is shaded light blue with the current cap formula and running maximum res shown below.

Step 1 only initializes, Steps 2 through 8 perform 7 capacity evaluations, and Step 9 exits when the pointers meet, so player step numbers do not equal capacity-evaluation counts. Below, the "Maximum capacity steps 2 to 8: calculations and running maximum" table summarizes each step; pointer indices, cap, and res are printed in the figure, while wall heights are read off the vertical axis.

frames.title: Initialize pointers at opposite ends
frames.explanation: Initialize left pointer i = 0 (wall height 3), right pointer j = 7 (wall height 4), and maximum capacity res = 0. No capacity has been evaluated yet, and no water region is shaded.
frames.key_state: Initialized: i = 0 (height 3), j = 7 (height 4), running maximum res = 0, current capacity not yet computed.
frames.announcement: Initialize two pointers at opposite ends i = 0, j = 7 with maximum capacity res = 0.

frames.title: Compute capacity of container [0, 7]
frames.explanation: First evaluation on outer pair [0, 7]: left wall ht[0] = 3, right wall ht[7] = 4, width 7 - 0 = 7, giving cap = min(3, 4) × 7 = 21 and updating res = max(0, 21) = 21. Because left wall 3 is shorter than right wall 4, move shorter-wall pointer i rightward next.
frames.key_state: i = 0 (height 3), j = 7 (height 4), left wall shorter; width 7, water height 3, cap = 21, running max res = 21.
frames.announcement: Evaluate outer walls: left height 3, right height 4, left shorter; cap = 21, update res to 21.

frames.title: Move shorter-wall pointer right to i = 1
frames.explanation: Because the left wall was shorter in the previous round, advance i from 0 to 1 for state [1, 7]: left wall ht[1] = 8, right wall ht[7] = 4, width 7 - 1 = 6, giving cap = min(8, 4) × 6 = 24 and updating res = max(21, 24) = 24. Now right wall 4 is shorter than left wall 8, so move right pointer j leftward next.
frames.key_state: i = 1 (height 8), j = 7 (height 4), right wall shorter; width 6, water height 4, cap = 24, running max res = 24.
frames.announcement: Move i from 0 to 1: left height 8, right height 4, right shorter; cap = 24, update res to 24.

frames.title: Move the right pointer left to j = 6
frames.explanation: Because right wall 4 was shorter than left wall 8, move j left from 7 to 6 for state [1, 6]: left wall 8, right wall ht[6] = 3, width 6 - 1 = 5, giving cap = min(8, 3) × 5 = 15; running maximum res = max(24, 15) = 24 stays unchanged.
frames.key_state: i = 1 (height 8), j = 6 (height 3), right wall shorter; width 5, water height 3, cap = 15, running max res = 24.
frames.announcement: Move j from 7 to 6: left height 8, right height 3, right shorter; cap = 15, res stays 24.

frames.title: Move the right pointer left to j = 5
frames.explanation: Because right wall 3 was shorter than left wall 8, move j left from 6 to 5 for state [1, 5]: left wall 8, right wall ht[5] = 7, width 5 - 1 = 4, giving cap = min(8, 7) × 4 = 28 and updating running maximum res = max(24, 28) = 28.
frames.key_state: i = 1 (height 8), j = 5 (height 7), right wall shorter; width 4, water height 7, cap = 28, running max res = 28.
frames.announcement: Move j from 6 to 5: left height 8, right height 7, right shorter; cap = 28, update res to 28.

frames.title: Move the right pointer left to j = 4
frames.explanation: Because right wall 7 was shorter than left wall 8, move j left from 5 to 4 for state [1, 4]: left wall 8, right wall ht[4] = 7, width 4 - 1 = 3, giving cap = min(8, 7) × 3 = 21; running maximum res = max(28, 21) = 28 stays unchanged.
frames.key_state: i = 1 (height 8), j = 4 (height 7), right wall shorter; width 3, water height 7, cap = 21, running max res = 28.
frames.announcement: Move j from 5 to 4: left height 8, right height 7, right shorter; cap = 21, res stays 28.

frames.title: Move the right pointer left to j = 3
frames.explanation: Because right wall 7 was shorter than left wall 8, move j left from 4 to 3 for state [1, 3]: left wall 8, right wall ht[3] = 2, width 3 - 1 = 2, giving cap = min(8, 2) × 2 = 4; running maximum res = max(28, 4) = 28 stays unchanged.
frames.key_state: i = 1 (height 8), j = 3 (height 2), right wall shorter; width 2, water height 2, cap = 4, running max res = 28.
frames.announcement: Move j from 4 to 3: left height 8, right height 2, right shorter; cap = 4, res stays 28.

frames.title: Move the right pointer left to j = 2
frames.explanation: Because right wall 2 was shorter than left wall 8, move j left from 3 to 2 for state [1, 2]: left wall 8, right wall ht[2] = 5, width 2 - 1 = 1, giving cap = min(8, 5) × 1 = 5; running maximum res = max(28, 5) = 28 stays unchanged.
frames.key_state: i = 1 (height 8), j = 2 (height 5), right wall shorter; width 1, water height 5, cap = 5, running max res = 28.
frames.announcement: Move j from 3 to 2: left height 8, right height 5, right shorter; cap = 5, res stays 28.

frames.title: Pointers meet and return maximum capacity
frames.explanation: Because right wall 5 is still shorter than left wall 8, j moves left from 2 to 1 and meets i. Above index 1, the two-color ij badge marks both pointers together (although axis tick 2 remains colored blue, it is no longer the current pointer position). Now i < j fails, so exit the loop without computing another capacity and return res = 28.
frames.key_state: Pointers meet at i = j = 1; exit the greedy loop and return maximum capacity res = 28.
frames.announcement: Right pointer moves left to index 1 to meet left pointer; exit loop and return maximum capacity 28.
